detail: raw exception normalised to UNEXPECTED_ERROR: Cannot convert 1.000 to a BigInt
note: A decimal with exactly three fractional digits followed by n lexes as a BIGINT token whose text still contains the dot, so PUSH_BIGINT reaches BigInt('1.000') and throws a raw SyntaxError, relabelled UNEXPECTED_ERROR/INTERNAL. 1.01n and 1.1n are fine, which points at the three-digit thousands-separator handling rather than at the n suffix. Distinct from the bytecode entry with the same normalised wording: that one needs a hand-built opcode stream, this one is six characters of ordinary source. FIXED at the source rather than at the crash. The lexer coalesces a group of exactly three digits after a "." or "," into the number it is building, and the two places that turned a BIGINT token into pool text (parser/PrecedenceParser.ts's Tier-1 switch and packages/biginteger/parselets/BigIntNumberParselet.ts) both stripped only the trailing "n", so the separators reached BigInt(). New parser/BigIntLiteral.ts is shared by both tiers: it strips the locale's own thousands separator (so 1,000n is 1000n in en) and chained dot groups (1.234.567n is 1234567n in any locale), and raises INVALID_NUMBER_LITERAL for a single dot group the locale reads as a decimal point, rather than guessing between 1 and 1000. vm/VM.ts's PUSH_BIGINT additionally parses through parseBigIntLiteral() as a backstop for the ./vm surface.
